# Light Water Capital

> Private capital management and family office based in Corydon, Indiana.

Light Water Capital is a private investment firm that manages capital for a select number of clients with a long-term, conviction-based approach. We combine quantitative research with fundamental judgment. We focus on public equities and quantitative strategies, building concentrated positions where we have high conviction.

## Recent Articles

- [Brazil Repriced Before the Bell](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-10-26-brazil-runoff-repricing/) - October 2026. How U.S.-listed Brazil assets traded on Monday, October 26, 2026, after incumbent Lula da Silva beat Flavio Bolsonaro 51.79% to 48.21% (official TSE result) in the October 25 presidential runoff. EWZ (iShares MSCI Brazil) opened 25.5% lower at $31.71, the largest opening gap in Polygon.io data back to September 2003 (the fund launched in 2000), hit a premarket low of $29.53 (-30.7%) at 4:14 a.m. ET, and closed down 19.8% at $34.15, its second-worst close in that data, on 299 million shares. EWZS fell 31.6%, FLBR 19.9%, ILF 11.2%, and BRZU (a 2x fund) 39.4%. In Sao Paulo, B3 halted trading with a 30-minute circuit breaker at the open (reopening auction 9:30-9:35 a.m. ET) and the Ibovespa closed down 13.88%. On indicative quotes, USD/BRL rose 8.3% from 4.99 to 5.40 between Friday and Monday 4 p.m. ET (real -7.7%; B3 reported the commercial dollar at R$5.40, +8.25%), while the Mexican, Chilean and Colombian pesos and the EWW/ECH/EPU country ETFs moved much less; Argentina's ARGT fell 4.9%. As a closing estimate on EWZ's market price, currency translation accounts for about 36% of its dollar loss on a log basis (implied decline in reais about 13.2%); the opening gap's split between stocks and currency cannot be measured from the available data. Among U.S.-listed Brazil shares and ADRs, XP fell 48.4%, Braskem 35.3%, Azul 32.6%, Bradesco 28.0%, StoneCo 27.4%, Itau 20.4% and Nu 17.0%, while exporters held up (Vale -3.2%, Suzano +2.1%). Covers Friday's pre-vote buying in Brazilian small caps, the stale indicative BRL feed, the reported legal challenge to the result, what the data cannot show, and what to watch (the real against B3's commercial-dollar close; the exporter-vs-financials spread). Context: Brazilian assets rallied after Bolsonaro led the October 4 first round about 47% to 45% (EWZ +12.5% and XP +30.9% on October 5; USD/BRL 5.22 to 5.00); late-campaign polls released October 19-21 showed him slightly ahead, and Polymarket contracts implied a 77% win probability on October 17 (AFP; contract-implied probabilities, not vote shares). Gross debt is forecast near 83% of GDP (Americas Quarterly). Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result over a court-ordered two-hour extension of voting at polling places still open (no confirmed court filing found as of the evening of October 26 ET). On Monday the January 2027 DI interest-rate future hit B3's daily limit, and the Treasury cancelled the week's inflation-linked and fixed-rate bond auctions and bought back about R$7.1 billion of bonds (UOL, InfoMoney). From October 2 to October 26, EWZ fell 10.6% and EEM 8.6% (an endpoint comparison, not a causal decomposition); Brazilian financials and small caps fell much further.
- [July Backtester v1.16: A Backtest That Is Harder to Flatter](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-10-24-july-backtester-v1-16/) - October 2026. Release announcement for July Backtester v1.16.0, Light Water's open-source Python backtesting engine. An adversarial backtest-integrity review found 17 verified defects (5 High, 6 Medium, 6 Low); the five High findings all biased results in the strategy's favor: gap-through stops filling at the stop level, no stop check on the fill bar under open execution, walk-forward normalized by initial capital, a Monte Carlo score that 200 of 200 zero-edge strategies passed, and equity shorts reserving no collateral. Covers the changed defaults and their compatibility settings, unified position sizing, point-in-time universes resolved to security IDs, new research scripts, and contributions from Shardul Mehetar, Angad Bhatti and Suriya Narayanan Rajavel.
- [Sugar Ran on Oil and Rain](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-10-21-sugar-oil-and-rain/) - October 2026. ICE raw sugar (No. 11) rallied more than 50% from a February low near 13.3 cents to a high near 21.3 cents in mid-October, its highest since early 2025, then went sideways on fading volume. Breaks the move into three legs: expensive oil, 14-cent sugar and Brazil's E32 blend pulling cane toward ethanol early in the season; weather, much of it tied to a possibly record El Niño, cutting crop forecasts in Brazil, India, Thailand and Europe at once; and managed-money positioning swinging from a 231,762-contract net short (Feb 17) to a 259,549 net long (Oct 13). Covers why the rally stalled (a narrowing March-May premium, a modest October delivery, cane carryover into 2027/28, soft demand and white-versus-raw tightness, India's ethanol tender excluding cane juice) and what to watch: the mid-October high, UNICA, ISMA, the CPC ENSO update and Hormuz.
- [Shardul Mehetar Named Lead Quantitative Research Intern](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-10-06-shardul-mehetar-lead-quantitative-research-intern/) - October 2026. Shardul Mehetar has been named Lead Quantitative Research Intern within Light Water's Systematic Strategies group, following two co-authored strategy evaluations, contributions to the July Backtester, and a seven-part empirical review of the firm's research assumptions.
- [Welcoming Our New Quantitative Strategy Intern](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-30-angad-bhatti-intern-announcement/) - September 2026. Angad Bhatti joins Light Water's Systematic Strategies team as a Quantitative Strategy Intern, auditing live equity strategies and developing new ones.
- [The Bonds Came Around](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-28-bonds-came-around/) - September 2026. On FOMC day long Treasuries rallied through the Fed's first hike in three years. About a week later they reversed: hot September flash PMIs, a hawkish Governor Barr and stalled US-Iran talks sent the 10-year Treasury to a 5.18% close on 24 September, its highest since July 2007, and the 30-year to 5.49%, above its 2006-07 peak. Covers the oil round-trip on Hormuz headlines (Brent under $100 on the Saudi pipeline restart, back above it when talks stalled, and a weekend rejection of Iran's reopening offer), the equity rotation into semiconductors while utilities, real estate and small caps repriced, and why the regime should be graded on the bond tape, not the stock index. What to watch: August PCE, Hormuz terms, and the dollar's breakout.
- [Everything Sold Off. Bonds Didn't.](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-16-everything-but-bonds/) - September 2026. The Fed hiked for the first time in three years and signaled at least one more this year. Stocks fell, oil was crushed, gold slid, the dollar rallied - the full fingerprint of a hawkish surprise. Long Treasuries rallied anyway.
- [The $100 Tax](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-10-the-100-tax/) - September 2026. Brent topped $100 as the Iran war hit Saudi refineries and the Strait of Hormuz - but crude rose 6% while the energy equities fell. Why the market is pricing triple-digit oil as a demand-destruction tax, not a producer windfall.
- [We Tested Seven Things Every Strategy Assumes](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-05-before-the-strategy-market-phenomena/) - September 2026. Seven foundational market phenomena, US equities back to 2004 - and the two statistical corrections that turned our best-looking results into nothing. By Shardul Mehetar.
- [The Labor Crack That Wasn't](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-09-04-labor-crack/) - September 2026. August payrolls came in at +162,000 against a ~53,000 estimate. Why the strong number nicked gold, spared stocks, and put a September rate hike back in play - and why the long bond barely moved.
- [The Bond Market Yawned: Warsh Talked Tough and the Market Shrugged](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/2026-08-28-warsh-yawn/) - August 2026. Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair was genuinely hawkish - and the bond market barely moved. Why the non-reaction is the signal, and where the hawkishness actually landed: the dollar.
- [Before a Single Bond: The Market Is Front-Running a Buyback That Hasn't Started](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/before-a-single-bond-august-2026/) - August 2026. Treasury announced an 'economic D-Day' on Iran and a doubled long-bond buyback in the same week. The dollar shrugged and oil fell; gold held near record highs. The tell is that the buyback hasn't bought a single bond yet - and gold is trading it anyway.
- [The Commodity Breakout That Isn't (Yet)](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/the-commodity-breakout-that-isnt-yet/) - August 2026. Fintwit called a multi-year cup-and-handle breakout on the Bloomberg Commodity Index. On the tape, its proxies are still 2-4% below their May highs - not through. Our read.
- [Nineteen Years: The 30-Year Treasury Makes a New Post-2007 High](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/thirty-year-treasury-2007-high-august-2026/) - August 2026. The 30-year Treasury yield topped 5.33% on 18 August, its highest since 2007, while the two-year fell to 4.18%. A bear steepener is a term-premium repricing, not a Fed repricing: covers the two components of a long yield, the supply arithmetic behind a ~$2.1 trillion projected FY2026 deficit, the 13 August 30-year auction clearing at 5.216%, AI hyperscaler bond issuance competing for long-duration capital, and the duration math that makes a "safe" long bond move like an equity.
- [The Clean Print: What July Core CPI Does - and Does Not - Change](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/the-clean-print-july-core-cpi-2026/) - August 2026. Core CPI cooled to 2.5% year over year and headline to 3.4%, but the print merely matched consensus. Covers the composition beneath the headline - shelter finally restrained at 0.1%, a mixed rather than broad-based core services basket, motor-vehicle insurance rolling over - and why an energy index still 14.7% higher than a year ago keeps this from being a regime change. Better is not the same as finished.
- [Boring Wins: DCA vs. Buying the Dip](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/boring-wins-dca-vs-buying-the-dip/) - August 2026. A popular rule says hold cash, wait for the Nasdaq to fall 10%, then buy your favorite names. Backtested on QQQ from 1999 to today: the bounce after a 10% dip is real at three and six months, but a standing weekly buy that never looks finished with roughly twice the wealth. The dip-buyer sat in cash 96% of the time. Also covers the survivorship trap in "your favorite stocks" - the index self-cleans, a single speculative name does not. By Zach Smith.
- [We Ran 60 Backtests on One Strategy. The Win Rate Never Beat a Coin Flip.](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/forex-ema-breakout-strategy-teardown/) - July 2026. A 50-EMA New York session breakout on EURUSD, GBPUSD and XAUUSD, tested across 16.5 years of hourly data and roughly 60 configurations - none with a real edge. Covers comparing win rate against the 1/(1+RR) breakeven instead of zero, separating gross from net expectancy to tell a cost problem from a signal problem, why higher-timeframe trend and volume filters made it worse, the "fewer trades looks better" trap, and a structural-stop bug that produced a single &minus;168R loss and negative equity. By Zach Smith and Shardul Mehetar. Full tearsheet PDFs available as downloads.
- [Warsh Draws the Line: Reading the July FOMC](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/warsh-fomc-july-2026/) - July 2026. The Fed held at 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote with all three dissenters wanting a hike, and Chair Kevin Warsh said this Fed "will not waver." The tell was the bond market: the Dow fell roughly 1,100 points while long Treasuries sold off rather than rallied, pushing the 30-year yield to its highest since 2007. Falling stocks plus falling bonds is an inflationary, higher-for-longer repricing - not a growth scare - and it explains why long-duration growth was punished while energy was the only green sector.
- [We Built a Trading Strategy Live. The First Result Was a +444% Mirage.](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/rsi-divergence-strategy-livestream/) - July 2026. A live-built RSI/price-divergence strategy on the Nasdaq 100 that first showed +444% and passed Monte Carlo and walk-forward checks - before we found it was almost entirely two stock-split data artifacts. A teardown of how a backtest lies before it tells the truth: split adjustment, Monte Carlo blind spots, winner-concentration testing, and the search for a real edge. By Zach Smith and Shardul Mehetar. Full tearsheet PDFs available as downloads.
- [Supply Scare, Demand Reality: Market Memorandum July 2026](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/dispatch/market-memorandum-july-2026/) - July 2026. The Iran ceasefire collapsed and crude spiked, but equities shrugged. A cross-asset read on the Strait of Hormuz supply shock, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve at a 40-year low, and the weakening demand picture capping the price.

Credit, banks, and commodities are not. A cross-asset read on SPY, oil, copper, credit, and the stagflation risk building beneath the surface. Full memorandum available as PDF download.

## Investment Philosophy

- Concentration over diversification: fewer, deeply researched positions
- Quantitative rigor: every thesis tested against data
- Long time horizons: underwriting investments over years, not quarters
- Aligned incentives: firm capital invested alongside clients

## Open Source

- July Backtester: https://github.com/zachisit/july-backtester - Professional-grade Python backtesting engine with Monte Carlo, walk-forward analysis, parameter sensitivity, and regime detection. MIT licensed.

## Open Roles

- [Quant Research & Strategy Intern](https://lightwaterdispatch.com/careers/quantitative-strategy-associate-internship/) - Remote, 20 hours/week, 3-month term with option to extend. Unpaid mentorship internship on the Systematic Strategies team. Audit the live common stock strategies for performance gaps and mathematical drift, then own new multi-asset strategies from thesis through to live deployment using in-house backtesting infrastructure and paid vendor data. Requires Python or a comparable data language, comfort with expectancy/variance/R-multiple distributions, and an active Claude or Codex subscription at the $20/month tier or above.
